clues.text: This high-flying coaster stands 113 feet tall, reaches a top speed of 62 mph, and flips riders through 6 inversions.
Built by renowned Swiss manufacturer B&M, the thrill ride first took flight in 1999.
Guests will find this coaster soaring over an amusement park in North Carolina.
This inverted coaster at Carowinds originally featured a military base aesthetic, with its main queue housed inside a hangar holding a two-thirds scale F-14 Tomcat fighter.
Its name refers to the fiery extra burst of thrust produced by a jet engine—or the lingering sting you feel after eating spicy wings.

evidence.quote: Afterburn is an inverted roller coaster located at Carowinds amusement park in Charlotte, North Carolina.
The main queue was housed in a hangar with a two-thirds scale F14 Tomcat fighter.
The aforementioned Top Gun roller coasters at other parks were all renamed to Flight Deck by the 2008 season, with Carowinds' installation being renamed to Afterburn.
